- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2), model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment-driven momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.1), model often overcorrects downward — avoid sharp drops; allow gradual reversion toward recent mean.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5-7 days — cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior high.  
- Model consistently underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price increases — adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.0% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model tends to lag — add 0.3–0.7% buffer to forecast to account for delayed reaction.  
- Avoid overfitting to recent 3–5 day highs — if forecast is above 3-day moving average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% to prevent over-optimism.
